subject.title: Exec allowlist matches never auto-execute on darwin — "allowlist auto-execution is unavailable on darwin; reviewer or explicit approval is required" (2026.6.11)

question: For macOS gateway exec, should shell-shaped allowlist matches be made enforceable and auto-executable, or should shell expansion remain approval-gated with clearer docs and warning text?
rationale: The reported behavior conflicts with the documented `on-miss` expectation, but the current gate protects a security boundary when command text cannot be rewritten into an enforceable plan.

options.title: Fix enforceable macOS shapes
options.body: Teach the POSIX authorization path to safely handle narrow cases such as home-prefix script paths while keeping genuinely unenforceable shell constructs approval-gated.

options.title: Document the limitation
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed approval behavior and document that shell expansion or wrapper quoting can require explicit approval even after an allowlist match.

options.title: Allow raw matched shell commands
options.body: Run matched shell-shaped commands without an enforced plan, restoring automation but accepting a larger shell-resolution security risk.

recommendation.title: Fix enforceable macOS shapes
recommendation.body: Teach the POSIX authorization path to safely handle narrow cases such as home-prefix script paths while keeping genuinely unenforceable shell constructs approval-gated.

likelyOwner.reason: Blame and merged PR history point to `vincentkoc` for the current gateway allowlist-plan gate and adjacent approval regression fixes.
